thread:
Alex: Quick heads-up — I want to enable the new burst autoscale toggle (enable_burst_v2) for the eu-west cluster next week. Planning: canary 5% traffic for 30m, then 25% for 2h if metrics look good. cc @Maria @Jay for guardrail checks.

Maria: Sounds ok, need to confirm two things: (1) scope = only public API routes or include internal batch jobs? (2) what roll-back thresholds are we using?

Alex: Good call. Scope = public endpoints only (route tag = public_api). Internal batch should be excluded. Rollback thresholds I was thinking: p99_latency > 800ms OR error_rate > 1.5% sustained for 5m. Open to tweaks.

Jay: +1 on scope. For guardrails, also enforce max_concurrency per worker = 48 during canary (prod default = 64). If queue_length > 120 or backlog_time > 60s we abort. We should also disable burst on nodes that are < 80% memory free.

Sam: Can you drop the PR/flag id here? I want to add the rollout window to the release calendar and ping approvers. Also need a short playbook for oncall to follow if we hit thresholds.

flags-bot: flag created: enable_burst_v2 (id: ff_8a3d). Initial state: off. Targeting config draft saved.

Alex: PR: https://git.redwood.com/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4321 — includes the rollout config and the canary scopes. Draft playbook in the PR description.

Maria: Taking a look now. A couple of suggestions inline: change p99 threshold to 750ms for eu-west (latency baseline slightly lower there), and add a metric for downstream throttling (RateLimit-4xx) to the abort conditions.

Jay: Agree re: 750ms. Also add a short delay between canary ramps: 5% -> wait 30m -> 25% -> wait 2h -> 50% -> wait 4h -> 100%. That gives us time to observe.

Alex: Updated the PR. Canary YAML (snippet):
```yaml
flag: enable_burst_v2
scopes:
  - region: eu-west
  - route_tag: public_api
canary:
  - pct: 5
    duration: 30m
  - pct: 25
    duration: 2h
  - pct: 50
    duration: 4h
rollbacks:
  - p99_latency_ms: 750
  - error_rate_pct: 1.5
  - rate_limit_4xx_pct: 0.5
  - queue_length: 120
  - backlog_seconds: 60
max_concurrency_per_worker: 48
memory_free_threshold_pct: 20
```

Sam: Nice. Oncall playbook notes: 1) If any rollback trigger fires, immediately set flag back to off and notify #incidents + paged oncall. 2) If p99 spike but no errors, slow the rollout (pause and extend observation). 3) If downstream 4xx spikes, roll back and open an investigation ticket. I'll copy this into the PR checklist.

Maria: One more: add a short-term metric bucket for token throughput to detect token storms — e.g., tokens_per_minute > historical_mean * 3 for 5m should also abort.

Alex: Added token-throughput rule to PR. Final question: canary audience — do we want to exclude a handful of customers (enterprise customers on dedicated infra)? I think yes.

Jay: Yes exclude dedicated enterprise customers. Add exclusion label: customer_type = dedicated. Also add annotation in flag: "manual_approval_required" = true before any global >50% ramp.

Alex: Done. I'll request final review from @Sam and @Maria. Targeting to start canary 2026-04-01 09:00 UTC (maintenance window) pending approvals.

Sam: LGTM, leaving final approval after PR checklist items are in. :thumbsup:

Maria: Approving once playbook and dashboards (p99, errors, queue, tokens, 4xx) are linked. I'll run the dashboards during first ramp.

flags-bot: rollout schedule saved for ff_8a3d, next action: enable 5% at 2026-04-01T09:00:00Z (pending manual approval).

Alex: Thanks everyone. I'll add a one-line announcement to #eng-all before the window and ping oncall 30m before start.

Sam: Ping me 30m before. I'll be on standby.

Jay: I'll keep an eye on infra metrics. If anything weird, I'll toggle back and open a postmortem.

Maria: Copy.

Alex: End of thread — will post updates in this thread during rollout.
